components.label: Caller · parent Pi agent
components.explanation: The caller here is the parent Pi agent using extension tools, not an HTTP client. subagent_spawn returns an ID after startup, without waiting for task completion. The parent may continue working, check status, explicitly wait, or receive an automatic follow-up. User-interface ingress and workflow delegation are outside this direct-tool slice.

components.label: Task & query tools
components.explanation: subagent_spawn accepts prompt/name plus optional role, cwd, model, worktree isolation and output schema. It validates cwd, applies plan-mode restrictions, resolves project trust, intersects child tools with the parent's active capabilities and sends a SpawnTask through runTool. check/list read manager snapshots; waitFor waits for settlement and returns results. A wait consumes pending automatic delivery; aborting a wait does not stop the child. Requested worktree creation fails closed rather than falling back to shared cwd.

components.label: SubagentManager
components.explanation: One shared Effect ManagedRuntime supplies the manager and production pi backend. The manager enforces pool limits and shared child-execution admission, creates a scoped backend session, allocates sa-N and stores the snapshot in an in-memory map. A scoped event pump folds activity and terminal evidence into that snapshot. Completion distinguishes completed, failed and interrupted outcomes; uncertain execution is separately represented. Subscribers and explicit waiters are notified; unconsumed settlements invoke the extension's onSettled hook. The live map is not a durable queue or external worker service.

components.label: Pi backend + child session
components.explanation: The production adapter creates a fresh Pi AgentSession with its own SessionManager, cwd-specific resources and tool policy, then starts session.prompt(task.prompt) asynchronously. Pi session events are translated into an Effect queue/stream for the manager. Terminal classification waits for the exact prompt promise to settle as well as checking lifecycle evidence, so agent_settled alone is not proof of success. The model and thinking level inherit from the parent unless explicitly overridden. Independence is session-level: by default the filesystem cwd is shared; this is neither a subprocess nor an OS sandbox. Pi SDK internals and durable session-file guarantees are not established by this checkout.

components.label: Completion delivery
components.explanation: onSettled records subagent-finished in the parent transcript, then defers a snapshot copy unless an explicit wait already consumed it. The inbox flushes immediately if the parent is idle, otherwise on the parent's agent_settled boundary. Explicit waits can consume pending envelopes to avoid duplicate automatic results. The dispatcher budgets output, appends a display entry and sends a hidden model-facing subagent-result followUp with triggerTurn=true. Oversized output may be saved in a content-addressed Pi cache artifact, with head/tail and a recovery locator; save failure is reported, not recast as execution failure. This inbox is in-process, not a message broker.

boundaries.label: OpenPI extension runtime · in-process calls and events

cards.title: Accept → return a handle
items: The parent chooses a task; spawn returns sa-N after startup, not completion.
check/list expose live snapshots; wait returns terminal output and consumes automatic delivery.

cards.title: Independent session ≠ sandbox
items: Child tools are narrowed; recursive subagent tools are excluded (shared/child-session.ts:514–527, 625–659).
Default cwd is shared. Optional worktree creation must succeed; no silent fallback (subagents/index.ts:1047–1061).

cards.title: Result evidence & limits
items: Status, execution outcome and persistence are distinct; session durability may be unknown (subagents/src/completion.ts:25–68).
Oversized output gets head/tail plus a cache path if saving succeeds (subagents/src/result-artifact.ts:110–164).
